assessment: Final post-swap pass at decklist 4a6369cc8929, floor 4: all six recommended swaps are applied, all six stacks still carry checker.verdict pass, and the 38-card bench is now doing exactly a bench's job — meta answers (Hellkite Tyrant, Transcendent Dragon, Balefire Dragon), detune pieces for lower-bracket tables (the six benched cuts, Sarkhan, Fireblood newest among them), and spares. One swap remains live, and it is deliberately conditional: Hellkite Tyrant over Thrakkus the Butcher when the pod is the Treasure/artifact-heavy one the pilot describes. Nothing else in the box upgrades this 99 under the standing bracket-4 max-power mandate, and saying so is the finding: the mandate's swap budget is spent because the evidence is spent, not because the diff got long.

swaps.when: Meta-conditional, unchanged across all three passes: sleeve it when the pod's 'token makers' are making Treasures, or against artifact-ramp piles — the pilot reports both are common; leave it boxed against low-artifact pods.
swaps.why: One connection from a 6/6 flying trampler takes every rock and Treasure the defending player controls — the theft line the pilot values, not the 20-artifact win this deck rarely reaches; Thrakkus stays the cut because doubling the power of an established attacking board is win-more in exactly the games where stealing a Treasure player's mana instead flips who is ahead, and the verified kills (stacks 001, 003, 006) never needed the stat multiplier.

opens_lines.why_plausible: Ventmaw's attack trigger adds {R}{R}{R}{G}{G}{G} that persists through steps and phases; the postcombat main phase pays Assault's {3}{R}{R} with {R} left over, untapping the team and buying another combat — self-sustaining, unbounded, +1 mana per cycle. Maindeck-contained.

Gnawbone mints Treasures equal to combat damage dealt to players, so any connection for 5+ funds the next activation — Gnawbone's own 7 power satisfies the condition standalone; on the verified board the engine table-kills over combats 6 and 12. Bounded only by Gnawbone's survival, flying/reach blockers, and the supply of opponents.

Every Dragon you control damaged by your own Act yields a redirect trigger even though it dies — LKI carries the 13 — so three Dragons throw 39 at non-Dragon targets while the sweep clears the table. One-sided punish that killed the 32-life opponent on the verified board; explicitly NOT a table-kill (kills one opponent at 39 or less).

For {R}, Drakuseth enters with haste, its attack trigger deals 4 plus 3 plus 3 before blockers, and all damage stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice; the commander-cheat reading stays refuted — Sneak Attack reaches only creature cards in hand, and Hellkite Courser is the deck's commander cheat.

The combo DB claims 'target opponent loses the game', but Cavern-Hoard only mints a Treasure per artifact the defending player controls — sustaining {3}{R}{R} per combat needs that opponent to keep five-plus artifacts on board. Meta-dependent (live in exactly the Treasure-heavy pods the pilot describes); the only maindeck-contained Assault line still unverified.

Sneak Attack's {R} activated ability has no timing restriction, and Wrathful only needs to be on the battlefield when the sweeper deals damage — cheating Wrathful in response to an opposing Blasphemous Act would extend verified stack 004 into a reactive ambush; the timing window and whether the redirect triggers all resolve before the end-step sacrifice matters are unverified.

Sneak Attack's delayed trigger sacrifices the creature it put onto the battlefield; Miirym's token copy is a separate object created by Miirym's own trigger — plausibly a permanent Dragon for {R}, a major rate if true. But most cheat targets are legendary, so the legend rule forces a choice, and which object the delayed trigger then finds is exactly a checker question.

long_term_defaults.why: Newly benched by the applied Atsushi swap. Comes back only in a bracket-3 detune where Aggravated Assault leaves the 99: with the plan reverted to casting the commander and 21 Dragons, its Dragon-spells-only {+1} for two mana is real turn-5-Ur-Dragon acceleration again, the rummage filters flooded hands, and the -7 is a fair-combat threat. In the bracket-4 list it is the sixth spells-only source that can never pay Assault's {3}{R}{R} — an activated ability is not a spell — and it stays boxed.

Benched cut. Comes back only as a detune: if a table declines bracket 4 and Aggravated Assault comes out, the fair-combat plan wants stats again and Crucible is the first anthem back in that slot. In the bracket-4 list its +3/+3 is redundant with kills that come from triggers (stack 001) and unbounded combats (stacks 003/006), not from size.

Benched cut. Its cut dropped cost-reducer availability from 43% to 34% by t6 (strategic_frame key tension) — if play experience shows Dragons landing a turn too slow, Servant is the first ramp piece back; it also returns in any bracket-3 detune where Korlessa's slot reverts. Until the goldfish shortfall shows up in real games, the seventh cost-reduction effect stays boxed.

Benched cut. Comes back against dedicated fast-combo pods where one-mana interaction density beats quality — countering a lethal win attempt makes the two-Treasure gift moot, and holding {U} on turn 2 is possible when holding {2}{R} is not. In the default pod, Deflecting Swat's slot does the same job without ramping the opponent.

Benched cut with the thinnest return case: it wants a deck whose instants and sorceries are the payoff, and this 99's spell suite is half ramp and protection — affinity discounts on Farseek are not power. Returns only if the list ever pivots toward a spell-dense build; no current configuration wants it back.

Benched cut. Comes back as the Sneak Attack replacement in a bracket-3 detune, where pure combat output without infinites is the point — and it is at its best while Thrakkus is still maindeck (the double-strike-on-doubled-power pairing the manual praised), so note that activating the Hellkite Tyrant swap removes half its return case.

The theft line is real — one connection takes a Treasure player's whole mana base — but it is a meta call, not a default: against low-artifact pods it is a 6/6 with no text. Sleeve it via the conditional swap when the pod's token makers are making Treasures.

Standing answer to the pilot: it is epic — a connection draws 10.5 cards on average with no maximum hand size — but the consistency half of the mandate cuts against another 8-drop on a curve whose core tension is its MV 5+ hump, and The Ur-Dragon's attack trigger already refills the hand from the same combat step without needing the connection. First card in if the play pattern turns out hellbent.

Aggravated Assault untaps creatures, not lands, so a full-colour Faeburrow re-taps for WUBRG every extra combat — but that is exactly one {R}, one short of self-funding the {3}{R}{R} reactivation, so it accelerates the verified engines without replacing their funding; it stays a non-Dragon that dies to the deck's own Blasphemous Act and Crux of Fate, and Chromatic Lantern plus The World Tree already patch the fixing gap.

Re-examined at the pilot's request and it stays out: its sweep hits each nonwhite creature, which includes nearly all of this deck's own Dragons — the white-less meta makes it better against their boards but does not spare ours. The pilot has seen this rationale.
Duplicate copy — Old Gnawbone is already in the 99 and a second copy is illegal in Commander. A spare, not an option.
Duplicate copy of a maindeck card; a spare, not an option.
Duplicate copy of a maindeck card; a spare, not an option.

The token-heavy meta makes it tempting — on connection it one-sidedly wipes the defending player's board — but maindeck Crux of Fate already destroys all non-Dragons at sorcery speed for five mana without surviving a combat first; it is the next conditional body in if the pod is multiple dedicated token decks at once.

Self-milling Dragons stocks the graveyard for maindeck Patriarch's Bidding, Haven of the Spirit Dragon, and Rivaz of the Claw, but the {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} cost is real against 9 white and 10 blue land sources.
A five-upkeep telegraphed alt-win that needs Dragons of all five colours on board; the indestructibility is the useful text, and Teferi's Protection plus Heroic Intervention already cover it.

Would re-fill the cost-reduction count the Servant cut lowered, but unlike the maindeck reducers it is not a Dragon for the typal payoffs — if that count needs repair, Dragonlord's Servant is the cheaper, on-type fix already sitting in the same box.

A fine two-mana dork whose {G} is at least unrestricted (it can pay Aggravated Assault, unlike the deck's five spells-only sources), but the deck already runs 15-plus ramp pieces and its bottleneck is cards, not mana.
Hellbent is anti-synergy in a deck that draws a card per attacking Dragon off the commander's battlefield trigger.
The tokens exile at end step, so they miss the deck's attack-trigger payoffs on any turn you cast a noncreature spell precombat and want to hold mana.
The deck casts few targeted spells — most triggers would come off its own removal, roughly one card per exchange.
The Omen face is a worse Farseek (basic to hand, not battlefield) and the creature face is a five-mana 3-power body in a deck full of better five-drops.

A flash Dragon that counters and exiles a spell is the right flex against spell-combo pods — a real conditional answer, but the 99's counterspell suite (Counterspell, Swan Song, Dovin's Veto, Deflecting Swat) covers the default pod.
Second-spell-each-turn copying wants a spell density this 21-Dragon curve does not produce; most turns cast one big thing.
Tapping three blockers for a turn is tempo the archetype does not need — its fliers are rarely blocked anyway.
The draw refill is gated on combat damage and a near-empty hand, and The Ur-Dragon's attack trigger already refills the hand the same way without the gate.
A hexproof-until-it-swings body with no other text; every maindeck Dragon at that cost carries a trigger.
Lifegain plus 5 damage to a non-flier across two castings is fine value but strictly less impactful than any current six-drop's trigger.
The 99 runs 23 instants and sorceries, but half are ramp, tutors, and protection — a free mid-combat Farseek is a whiff, and the payoff needs that whiff rate priced in.
Wants a Dragon-storm turn the curve produces rarely, and its damage cannot hit commanders — the target that matters most at this table.
An instant/sorcery payoff in a creature deck; wrong 99 for its trigger.
+1/+0 to one creature per combat is the weakest text in the box; the Omen face's 2/2 Soldier is not a Dragon.
The spell density won't sustain it, and maindeck Utvara Hellkite already makes bigger Dragon tokens off the attack the deck makes every turn.
A Phyrexian-mana pump wincon built for a Scion voltron shell; in this deck it is a vanilla 4/4 flier for four-ish.
Anthems only red and white creatures in a five-colour deck, and {2}{R/W}{R/W}{R/W} is a hostile cost on 9 white sources.
Retaining red mana across phases slightly extends Savage Ventmaw's trigger, but Ventmaw's own text already holds the mana through end of turn — a win-more wrinkle, not a slot.

Exert removal is real, but the deck already runs 9-plus removal pieces and the exert un-untap directly fights the maindeck Aggravated Assault extra-combat plan — it exerts out of the very untap the engine buys.
Often nearly free with a Dragon board, but the deck has no self-mill to exploit the graveyard recursion, and a late vanilla beater is what the deck already has most of.

gaps: Cavern-Hoard Dragon + Aggravated Assault is the only maindeck-contained Assault line without a stack artifact; a scenario would settle whether its artifact-count-dependent funding counts for anything in the pilot's Treasure-heavy pods.

The two frame candidates — Sneak Attack at instant speed in response to a sweeper (extending stack 004), and whether a Miirym token copy survives Sneak Attack's end-step sacrifice — both need stack scenarios before either line is claimed anywhere; the Miirym one also has to resolve the legend rule on legendary cheat targets.

The strategy corpus has no section on cheat-into-play vectors or extra-combat chaining (both recorded strategic_frame gaps), so the Hellkite Tyrant swap is argued from oracle text and the pilot's meta report, with no citation to attach.

14 maindeck cards have no card_roles.json entry (deck-facts note), so role-count claims ('15-plus ramp pieces', '9-plus removal pieces') are floors, not exact counts.

Whether the Dragonlord's Servant cut's cost-reducer drop (43% to 34% by t6) matters in practice is unmeasurable from goldfish alone — its return case waits on play experience, not on data this pass can compute.
